title: W32.Stuxnet Dossier, Version 1.4
quality_rationale: Primary technical reverse-engineering of the worm: four zero-days, PLC injection, frequency manipulation, and operator deception.
excerpt: Stuxnet represents the first of many milestones in malicious code history - it is the first to exploit four 0-day vulnerabilities compromise two digital certificates and inject code into industrial control systems and hide the code from the operator.

title: The Real Story of Stuxnet
quality_rationale: Technology feature describing 500 KB worm, 14 Iranian industrial sites, USB air-gap crossing, four zero-days, and ~1,000 destroyed centrifuges.
excerpt: a 500-kilobyte computer worm that infected the software of at least 14 industrial sites in Iran, including a uranium-enrichment plant.

title: Stuxnet Analysis
quality_rationale: EU agency technical explainer: targets Siemens SIMATIC WinCC/STEP 7 SCADA, spreads via USB drives or open network shares.
excerpt: Stuxnet is a specialised malware targeting SCADA systems running Siemens SIMATIC WinCC or SIMATIC Siemens STEP 7 software for process visualisation and system control.

title: Did Stuxnet Take Out 1,000 Centrifuges at the Natanz Enrichment Plant?
publisher: Institute for Science and International Security
quality_rationale: Nuclear-security analysis of IAEA data: about 1,000 IR-1 centrifuges replaced at Natanz; says Stuxnet could explain the breakage.
excerpt: In late 2009 or early 2010, Iran decommissioned and replaced about 1,000 IR-1 centrifuges in the Fuel Enrichment Plant (FEP) at Natanz, implying that these centrifuges broke.

title: The Stuxnet Computer Worm: Harbinger of an Emerging Warfare Capability
quality_rationale: Official CRS report: thumb-drive infection, worldwide spread, and contemporaneous caution that the actual target was unknown.
excerpt: Through the use of thumb drives in computers that were not connected to the Internet, a malicious software program known as Stuxnet infected computer systems that were used to control the functioning of a nuclear power plant.

title: US and Israel were behind Stuxnet claims researcher
quality_rationale: Early attribution claim by Ralph Langner; records that there was no hard evidence at the time.
excerpt: Israel and the United States created the Stuxnet worm to sabotage Iran's nuclear programme, a leading security expert has claimed.

title: NSA leaker Snowden claimed U.S. and Israel co-wrote Stuxnet virus
